question: Micturating cystourethrography (MCUG) is the definitive investigation for grading vesicoureteric reflux (VUR), with grades I–V based on the height and degree of pelvicalyceal dilatation seen during voiding.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is TRUE. MCUG is the definitive test for VUR grading. Grades I–V describe the extent of reflux and pelvicalyceal dilatation during voiding. This grading directly guides management decisions (prophylaxis vs surgery).
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. MCUG is the gold-standard for VUR grading. Grade I = reflux into ureter only; Grade V = gross dilatation with ureteric tortuosity and loss of papillary impression. Ultrasound can suggest dilated systems but cannot grade VUR.
